question: If a man travels 200 km. each at three speeds of 60, 50 and 40 km/h. respectively, then his average speed is:
solution:
The correct answer is** 48.65 km/h**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__** Average Speed Calculation:

__
 
• Average speed is calculated by dividing the total distance traveled by the total time taken.
 
• In this case, the man travels 200 km at each speed of 60 km/h, 50 km/h, and 40 km/h.
 
• **Time taken for each segment:**
 
 
• Time at 60 km/h = 200 km / 60 km/h = 3.33 hours
 
• Time at 50 km/h = 200 km / 50 km/h = 4 hours
 
• Time at 40 km/h = 200 km / 40 km/h = 5 hours
 
 
 
• Total time taken = 3.33 + 4 + 5 = 12.33 hours
 
• Total distance traveled = 200 km + 200 km + 200 km = 600 km
 
• Average speed = Total distance / Total time = 600 km / 12.33 hours ≈ 48.65 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 Explanation of Incorrect Options:

 
• Option 1: 47.65 km/h - This is incorrect because it does not accurately account for the total time taken.
 
• Option 2: 49.45 km/h - This is incorrect because it overestimates the average speed.
 
• Option 3: 48 km/h - This is close but slightly underestimates the correct average speed.
 
• Option 4: 48.65 km/h - This is the correct answer as it accurately reflects the total distance and time calculations.
